title: Netflix Co-CEOs Address Executive Shakeup and Layoffs in Town Hall, Deadline Reveals
body:
Netflix’s co‑chief executives, Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters, convened a company‑wide town hall on Wednesday to address a wave of executive departures and the latest round of staff reductions, while also underscoring confidence in the newly appointed chief content officer, Peter Rice. The meeting came just a day after the streaming giant’s third‑quarter earnings call, where investors expressed unease over mixed financial results and a slower subscriber growth trajectory. By speaking directly to employees, the leadership aimed to steady internal morale and signal a clear strategic direction amid the turbulence.

The town hall opened with Sarandos acknowledging the “significant transition” the organization has undergone in recent months. Since the start of the year, Netflix has seen a cascade of senior exits, including the departures of several regional heads and long‑standing members of the content acquisition team. In tandem, the company announced another round of layoffs affecting roughly 150 employees across product, marketing and finance functions. While the cuts represent a modest percentage of the overall workforce, they are the latest in a series of cost‑containment measures that began in early 2023 and have intensified as the firm grapples with rising competition and a more price‑sensitive subscriber base.

Peters shifted the focus to the newly hired chief content officer, Peter Rice, highlighting his extensive background in both scripted and unscripted programming. Rice, who previously led content strategy at a major European broadcaster and oversaw award‑winning series at a leading streaming platform, is tasked with revitalizing Netflix’s content pipeline and sharpening its global storytelling edge. Sarandos emphasized that Rice’s “track record of delivering high‑impact, culturally resonant series” aligns with Netflix’s ambition to sustain a differentiated library that can attract and retain viewers in an increasingly crowded market.

Analysts have been closely watching how Netflix’s leadership reshapes its content strategy after a period of aggressive spending on high‑budget productions that failed to deliver the expected subscriber lift. The company’s Q3 report revealed a modest 2.2 percent increase in global memberships, well below the growth rates seen in previous years, and a dip in average revenue per user (ARPU) in key markets. By placing a seasoned content veteran at the helm, Netflix hopes to balance ambitious creative goals with tighter fiscal discipline, prioritizing projects that promise both critical acclaim and broad audience appeal.

Employees in the virtual session were given the opportunity to pose questions, many of which centered on job security, the timeline for further restructuring, and the future of the company’s original‑content slate. Sarandos and Peters responded by reiterating a “long‑term vision” that includes continued investment in original storytelling, but with a more data‑driven approach to greenlighting projects. They also promised transparent communication about any additional workforce changes, noting that the current reductions are intended to “streamline operations and eliminate redundancies” rather than signal a broader downsizing wave.

The town hall concluded with a reaffirmation of Netflix’s commitment to its core mission: delivering compelling, diverse entertainment to a global audience. While the leadership acknowledges the challenges posed by slowing growth and heightened competition from rivals such as Disney+, HBO Max and emerging regional platforms, they expressed confidence that the new content leadership and a leaner organizational structure will enable the company to adapt more swiftly to shifting consumer preferences.

Looking ahead, industry observers will be watching how quickly Peter Rice can translate his experience into a refreshed slate of shows and films that resonate with both existing subscribers and new audiences. If Netflix can successfully align its creative ambitions with disciplined financial management, the streaming pioneer may yet regain the momentum that once defined its rapid ascent, positioning itself for sustainable growth in the evolving entertainment landscape.
